## Yamaha Serial 0.2.2

A maintenance release for ESPHome 2026.10. No component code changed: the
C++ and the Python code generation are byte-for-byte those of `v0.2.1`. What
changed is the examples, the stated baseline, and one credential.

### Changed

**The examples authenticate OTA with the API encryption key.** They used to
carry both an `api: encryption: key:` and a separate `ota: password:`.
ESPHome reports the password as roughly 3.5 KB of flash and 60 bytes of RAM
on a device that already holds a key which authenticates any uploader that
has it. Measured on the ESP8266 full example, which is compiled against a
size budget in CI, dropping it saves 3 256 bytes of flash and 32 bytes of
RAM. `ota_password` is gone from
`examples/secrets.example.yaml`, and `esphome config` on all three examples
is now warning-free.

```yaml
ota:
  - platform: esphome
    encryption:          # inherits the one key per device from api:
```

**Adopting it on a running device is an ordinary OTA install.** The
examples have always configured `api: encryption: key:`, and the OTA
component takes its key from that block: it offers encrypted OTA whenever a
key is present anywhere, and an `ota: encryption:` block only adds the
*requirement*. A device built from `v0.2.0` or `v0.2.1` therefore already
speaks the encrypted protocol, and once a session is negotiated the device
goes straight to the data phase without ever asking for the password. No
serial flash, no two-step.

The two-step procedure in the
[ESPHome documentation](https://esphome.io/components/ota/esphome/#enabling-encryption-on-an-existing-device)
is for firmware that offers no encryption at all — not the case here,
because the API key was always part of these examples. Doing nothing is also
fine: a password build keeps working, it is only larger than it needs to
be.

### Compatibility

The validated baseline is now ESPHome `2026.10.x`. The minimum stays
`2026.9.0`; it is bumped by hand and this release does not move it.

2026.10.0 switches the ESP8266 build from PlatformIO to the native Arduino
toolchain. Both examples compile green on it, and the full example got
smaller in the process:

| ESP8266 full example | Flash | RAM |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.2.1` on 2026.9.1 | 483 823 | 59 440 |
| the same source on 2026.10.0 | 478 564 | 58 764 |
| `v0.2.2` on 2026.10.0 | 475 308 | 58 732 |

The middle row isolates the toolchain: it is `v0.2.1`'s configuration built
by 2026.10.0. The last row adds this release's dropped OTA password.

Two 2026.10 breaking changes look like they touch this component and do not.
`select` options moved into a flash-backed `ConstVector` and `SelectTraits`
became non-copyable; the component passes a `FixedVector<const char *>` to an
overload that still exists and never reads `get_options()`. And
`media_player.h` is byte-identical between 2026.9.1 and 2026.10.0, so the
missing source and sound-mode values in the call path are unchanged — the
`select` entities and the optional Home Assistant companion remain the
supported route for source and DSP program.

### Installation

```yaml
external_components:
  - source: github://memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial@v0.2.2
    components: [yamaha_serial]
```

Requires ESPHome 2026.9.0 or newer. The full changelog is in
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
